title: Lithuania moves Switchblade 600 capability from procurement into reported warehouse receipt before use or deterrence is visible
source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of the first Switchblade 600 shipment
geography: Lithuania; Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses; United States–Lithuania defense-supply relationship

delivery_stage.value: the first shipment of U.S.-made Switchblade 600 loitering munitions supplied by AeroVironment reached Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses

support_equipment.value: launch and control equipment, a personnel-training simulator, and a maintenance package reported alongside the munitions

stated_capability.value: long-range, precision, anti-armour strike capability described by the ministry

stated_security_meaning.value: official claims that the acquisition strengthens deterrence, Lithuanian security, and the Lithuania–United States partnership

use_and_effect.unit: missing quantity, cost, acceptance, inventory allocation, training completion, maintenance readiness, field deployment, operational use, deterrence, adversary response, civilian protection, and public judgment

mechanism.value: A warehouse receipt converts a procurement commitment into reported possession and a possible capability pathway, but possession is not fielded readiness or demonstrated deterrence.

observations.method: Structured extraction from the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence announcement. Receipt, support equipment, stated capability and purpose, and unmeasured operational and civilian outcomes are coded as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not disclose shipment quantity, unit cost, acceptance records, inventory allocation, training completion, maintenance readiness, field deployment, operational use, incident effects, deterrence, adversary adaptation, or civilian protection.
observations.subgroup: Lithuanian Armed Forces, defense suppliers and maintainers, Lithuanian and U.S. defense institutions, allied forces, and civilians potentially affected by future deployment; no affected-person denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Receipt may strengthen future readiness and alliance interoperability, while stored equipment can remain unused or impose fiscal, maintenance, escalation, and civilian-risk costs that the announcement does not measure.

related_sources.claim: Earlier procurement reporting describes the acquisition path; it is background to the later receipt and not evidence of use or readiness.

boundary: This record establishes a reported first shipment of Switchblade 600 systems and associated support equipment reaching Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses. It does not establish quantity, acceptance, training, deployment, operational use, deterrence, adversary response, civilian protection, or public legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project follow-up memo derived from the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence source; procurement files, inventory records, training logs, and operational telemetry are not retained.
